dedupe_keys.name: urbalytics remote sensing layers for urban heat risk and green infrastructure cooling milan and naples 2018 2022

description: UrbAlytics is an experimental sub-project of the EU Horizon 2020 AI4Copernicus project that uses Earth observation and artificial intelligence to produce information layers on the urban heat island effect for city planners, assess ecosystem services of blue and green infrastructure and propose nature-based solutions for extreme heat mitigation. This dataset is the output of its fully automated workflow for the pilot cities of Milan and Naples over 2018 to 2022. Layers include a Heatwave Potential Risk index from 0 to 1 combining heat island severity, exposure of sensitive age groups and vulnerability from city morphology and surface materials, and a Microclimatic Performance Index estimating the cooling potential of urban vegetation from machine-learning tree cover density and land cover maps. It was produced by Latitudo 40 and LAND Italia researchers and published on Zenodo in September 2023 as a single downloadable ZIP file (about 27 MB); Zenodo lists the licence as other (attribution). Caveats: the layers cover two cities and the deposit holds output layers only, not the workflow code. It supports climate adaptation, heat hazard exposure mapping and siting of green infrastructure; a related record is the Helsinki urban heat vulnerability index.
name: UrbAlytics remote sensing layers for urban heat risk and green infrastructure cooling (Milan and Naples, 2018-2022)
notes: Reference: Giacco, G. et al. (2023). UrbAlytics - Remote Sensing tools for Urban Heat Island Assessment and Climate Change Adaptation through Nature-Based Solutions. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.8321140
